guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for individual connected users. The app must be registered first to obtain a client ID and secret. The narrowest documented read scope covering the issues API is read_api, which grants read access to the API including all groups and projects the connected person can access. Issue listing is documented for authenticated users and supports keyset and offset pagination. Access tokens expire by default after two hours and use refresh tokens. Distribution to other customer organizations is not covered by the supplied sources.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API for accessible projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, and is sufficient for queries. It is read-only, so it cannot be used for issue creation, update or deletion. Its boundary is the projects the connected person can access.

findings.detail: After saving the application, GitLab provides the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret. The secret must be kept secure and is needed for the authorization code exchange.

steps.title: Register GitLab OAuth application for connected users
steps.detail: A developer registers a user-owned GitLab OAuth application in the GitLab UI so individual users can authorize access. Save the Application ID (client ID) and Client Secret. Use a redirect URI that the customer's application controls; use HTTPS in production.
steps.doneWhen: Application is saved and the Application ID and Client Secret are stored securely for the test. No consent or token has been obtained.

Enter a Name and Redirect URI .

fields: Application ID: provided by GitLab after saving the application

steps.title: Individual user consent via authorization code flow
steps.detail: The connected GitLab user opens the authorization URL in a browser, reviews the requested read_api scope and approves. GitLab redirects to the redirect URI with a code and state. The customer app must check that state matches before exchanging the code. This is a manual user action; the agent does not perform it.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect callback returns a code and a matching state value. No token exchange has occurred yet.

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for access token
steps.detail: After consent, the customer app exchanges the returned code at the documented token endpoint using the client secret, grant_type authorization_code and the same redirect_uri. Send client credentials either as parameters or Basic auth, not both. The response contains access_token and refresh_token; expires_in is 7200 by default.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token; the token value is stored securely and not logged.

steps.title: Read first page of project issue titles
steps.detail: Using the access token, list issues for one representative project the connected person can access. Map the user's requested value to the title property of each object in the returned JSON array. Use a project ID that the developer supplies with provenance (for example, the project they already have access to). Return up to 20 results per page by default.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array; each object's title property is readable. The response Link header is recorded if present. steps.title: Read next page of issue titles via Link header
steps.detail: Follow the rel="next" URL from the Link header of the prior response. Resolve any relative href against the same HTTPS instance host. Continue until the Link header lacks a rel="next" entry; that is the documented end condition. Do not build the URL manually; use only the given link. The documented end condition is that the Link header is absent or has no rel="next" entry; the resulting array may then be empty. Record the final page for completeness.
steps.doneWhen: The next page returns HTTP 200 and the absence of rel="next" in the Link header is recorded as the end of the listing. The final response has no rel="next" link and its array is empty or ends the listing. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
